🚨 **BREAKING**: Elon Musk is planning an unprecedented move for retail investors in the SpaceX IPO!

He’s considering allocating **up to 30%** of SpaceX’s IPO to retail investors — triple the typical 5-10% — per Reuters.

The goal? To tap his loyal fans in what could be a **$1.75 trillion** valuation IPO.

Elon is taking a hands-on approach with banks, assigning them specific roles instead of broad competition. Bank of America is expected to lead U.S. retail distribution, alongside Morgan Stanley and UBS.

The biggest IPO in history is prioritizing retail! 🚀

David Moss (@DavidMoss) — 28-year-old LiDAR salesman (yes, the guy who sells the very hardware Tesla doesn’t use) — just completed the first verified zero-intervention coast-to-coast Tesla FSD drive in history

2,732 miles.  
LA Tesla Diner → Myrtle Beach, SC.  
FSD v14.2 Supervised.  
ZERO disengagements. Not one single touch of the wheel or pedals — not in traffic, not at Superchargers, not even pulling in to park.

This wasn’t a fluke. It’s part of his 12,961-mile** intervention-free streak, all logged and verified by the FSD Database.

Tesla just dropped his story on their official customer page today.

The irony of a LiDAR pro trusting vision-only FSD this hard? Chef’s kiss. This is exactly how real autonomy wins — one impossible drive at a time.

Absolute legend, David. The rest of the industry is watching.  

@Tesla @Tesla_AI @robotaxi

Don’t bet against Elon Musk making data centers in space 

“Never ever bet against Elon Musk. 

He's the greatest entrepreneur of our generation. 

The man has averaged the creation of a multibillion-dollar company every five years for over 30 years.

There's no one in history who has ever done this before. 

A huge reason why he is so competitive in the marketplace is because he is willing to take an enormous amount of risk and go after very ambitious things. 

Building data centers in space sounds crazy until you realize that he has already launched thousands of satellites. 

He's already built a reusable rocket. 

Putting the data centers in space may actually be a much less hard task to do than the things that he's already done. 

And so I definitely think that he's going to pull this off.”
